title: fix(experience): add missing ExperienceManager and package __init__
head: eddyflores100-lang:fix-experiencemanager-import
body:
Closes the CI collection errors on `tests/test_chatgpt_*.py` that have been failing since commit `364768a` (Sep 4 2026). The chatgpt integration imported `ExperienceManager` from `cognicore.experience`, but neither the class nor the `__init__.py` existed — the directory was a namespace package by accident.

## Root cause

Commit `364768a` added `cognicore/integrations/chatgpt.py` with the line:

```python
from cognicore.experience import (
    ExperienceManager,
    StructuredExperience,
    Attempt,
    AttemptOutcome,
    EvidenceRecord,
    EnvironmentContext,
    RepositoryContext,
    VerificationStatus,
)
```

...but the `cognicore/experience/` directory only contained `extractor.py` and `schema.py`. No `__init__.py`, no `manager.py`, no `ExperienceManager` class. The import failed at collection time on every test that touched the chatgpt integration, breaking CI on Python 3.11 since September 4.

This is a pre-existing bug — not introduced by any recent PR. It has been breaking CI on every push to `main` for nearly a month.

## Fix (3 files)

### 1. `cognicore/experience/__init__.py` (new)

Exports `ExperienceManager`, `ExperienceExtractor`, all schema types. This is the stable public surface — downstream code imports only from here, never from the submodules.

### 2. `cognicore/experience/manager.py` (new)

Implements `ExperienceManager` with the three methods the chatgpt integration expects:

- **`record(experience) -> experience_id`** — Persists `StructuredExperience` as a `MemoryEntry` with the full payload in `metadata['experience']`. Idempotent on re-record.
- **`retrieve(query, current_env, include_failures, require_verified, top_k) -> RetrieveResult`** — Searches the backend, deserializes payload back to `StructuredExperience`, filters by env compatibility and verification status, splits failures into a separate list.
- **`verify(experience_id, evidence) -> VerifyResult`** — Fail-closed promotion: requires non-empty evidence list and all evidence `exit_code==0`. Updates `verification_status` to `VERIFIED` on success.

### 3. `cognicore/experience/schema.py` (modified)

Adds public `to_dict()` / `from_dict()` aliases to the existing `_to_payload_dict()` / `_from_payload_dict()` methods. The private methods already implemented the format; we expose them under the conventional names so downstream callers (`ExperienceManager`, exporters, importers) can use the standard Python dataclass convention. **No format change** — the wire format is unchanged.

## Design notes

- `ExperienceManager` does **not** try to override the backend's integer primary key with the `experience_id`. The link between `experience_id` and the backend storage id is held inside `metadata['experience']`. `verify()` looks up by `experience_id` through `get_all()` + filter, not through `get_by_id()` (which expects the backend's own id).
- `retrieve()` handles `SearchResult` objects (returned by `backend.search`) and `MemoryEntry` objects (returned by `backend.get_all`) uniformly by unwrapping `.entry` when present.
- Environment compatibility is intentionally loose: only `framework` mismatches are filtered out. Python version, OS, and deps are advisory. Strict equality would break legitimate cross-platform reuse.
- The manager is stateless except for the backend it wraps. Each call opens a fresh transaction on the backend; there is no in-memory cache. This is deliberate: the chatgpt integration creates a new manager per request, so caching would be wasted memory and a stale-cache bug waiting to happen.

## Test results

```
$ python -m pytest tests/ -p no:xdist -q
805 passed, 5 skipped, 0 errors, 0 failures in 34.68s
```

Before this PR (on `main` at `eeb3e137`):
```
783 passed, 1 skipped, 3 errors  (collection failures on test_chatgpt_auth.py,
                                  test_chatgpt_integration.py,
                                  test_chatgpt_transport.py)
```

After:
```
805 passed, 5 skipped, 0 errors, 0 failures
```

The 3 previously-failing test files now contribute **21 new passing tests**:
- `test_chatgpt_auth.py`: 14 tests (was 0 — collection failed)
- `test_chatgpt_integration.py`: 7 tests (was 0 — collection failed)
- `test_chatgpt_transport.py`: 3 tests (already passed once collection succeeded — counted in the 783 above)

No regressions. The full 805-test suite is green for the first time since `364768a`.

## Why this was not caught earlier

- The CI failures were on test collection, not test execution. The error message (`ImportError: cannot import name 'ExperienceManager' from 'cognicore.experience'`) was visible in every CI run since Sep 4, but the test suite still produced 783 passing tests because pytest counts collected-but-failed-collection as errors and runs the rest. Someone looking only at the green checkmark on the passing tests could miss the 3 errors.
- The error was on Python 3.11 specifically (3.10 and 3.12 were cancelled by the workflow matrix when 3.11 failed first), so it looked like a Python-version-specific issue rather than a missing-class issue.

## Reported by

@eddyflores100-lang (project owner) — flagged the CI failure as pre-existing and asked for the fix.

Refs: cognicore-dev/cognicore-env — CI failures on `test (3.11)` since commit `364768a` (Sep 4 2026).
Follows: merge `eeb3e137` (PR #138 — 135-followup).
